issues.description: Predicate `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is over-broad and reads as a double negative
issues.detail: The guard fires for any non-Tab key when the option is off, not just Enter/Return as the option name implies. This silently changes behavior for any other key that reaches this branch. Restate the policy explicitly as `key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter) and not use_enter_for_completions`, or lift an accept-keys set as data and test membership. Also replace `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` with `key != Qt.Key_Tab` for clarity.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the QKeyEvent directly to `textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` bypasses Qt event propagation
issues.detail: Calling `self.hide(); self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` manually forwards a consumed event into a sibling widget's handler, bypassing Qt's normal accepted/ignored state, focus routing, and input-method composition. No invariant is stated about reentrancy or event state. Prefer `event.ignore()` plus `self.hide()` so the event propagates through the standard channel.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keystroke in the popup instead of cached on the widget
issues.detail: `self.get_conf('use_enter_for_completions', section='completions')` runs inside keyPressEvent and is re-fetched per key. The value changes only when the preference changes, so it should be cached on the widget (e.g. `self._accept_with_enter`) and refreshed via a config-change signal. This both shrinks the handler body and removes a hot-path config lookup.

issues.description: No tests cover the new behavior
issues.detail: The diff adds a new user-facing option that changes a keypress code path with zero test coverage. A small test exercising Return, Enter, and Tab under both states of `use_enter_for_completions` would document the intended invariant and prevent silent regression on future refactors of keyPressEvent.

issues.description: New branch lacks a literate comment / stated contract
issues.detail: The new block has no comment naming the option, the keys it governs, or why the event is re-dispatched. A two-line comment stating the precondition and postcondition (e.g. 'when Enter-to-accept is off, forward Enter/Return to the editor; Tab still accepts') would make the code self-documenting and lock in the intended contract for future maintainers.

issues.description: User-facing label/tip and implemented predicate disagree on semantics
issues.detail: The UI label says 'Use Enter to accept code completions' and the tip mentions Tab, but the implemented predicate forwards every non-Tab key when the option is off. The spec ('Enter vs Tab') and the implementation ('Tab vs everything-else') are not the same statement. Either tighten the predicate to Enter/Return or correct the user-facing copy so they agree.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear verdict: the intent is right and the surface area is small, but the four-line guard inside `keyPressEvent` is poorly shaped. The predicate `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is a double negative that is also too permissive — it fires for any non-Tab key rather than just Enter/Return — and it reads the config on every keystroke. Re-dispatching the QKeyEvent directly to `textedit.keyPressEvent` smuggles the event past Qt's normal propagation and should be replaced with `event.ignore()`. The change also lands without tests, without a literate comment stating the invariant, and with UI copy that does not match the implemented behavior. Fix the predicate (lift to an explicit Enter/Return check or an accept-keys set, cache the config value on the widget), use standard event propagation, and add at least one test covering Return/Enter/Tab under both option states.
